name: Imaging and Digital Pathology AI

title: Imaging and Digital Pathology AI
answer: Imaging is where most authorized AI devices sit, and digital pathology is following as slides are scanned and foundation models are trained on them. Pathology AI companies are raising growth capital and working with most large drugmakers on biomarker discovery as well as diagnosis.

reading.body:
Radiology still holds the majority of FDA-listed AI devices, and pathology is the next imaging specialty to watch as slides get digitised.

The pattern is that imaging is where authorized AI devices concentrate, and pathology follows the same path once scanning is in place. Proscia's $50 million raise in 2025 is growth capital aimed at AI-driven pathology and precision medicine, which suggests investors expect the scanning prerequisite to be met at scale rather than in pilot sites.

For AI specifically, the constraint is not the model but the input. A pathology foundation model needs whole slides in digital form before it can be trained or deployed, so the value arrives after the scanning programme, not alongside it. The same logic that put radiology first applies here: the specialty that digitised earliest accumulated the data and the clearances.

What this does not cover is how many pathology devices are authorized, how far scanning has spread across laboratories, or whether the drugmaker partnerships on biomarker discovery have produced anything durable. The evidence here is one funding round and one count from the FDA list, which is enough to establish direction and not enough to size the market.

explainer:
Medical imaging AI reads X-rays, CT, MRI, mammograms and other scans to detect findings, measure structures, prioritise urgent cases and reduce reporting time. It is the largest category of authorised AI devices because images are plentiful, digital and paired with reports.

Pathology is following. Glass slides of tissue are being digitised into whole slide images, which lets AI help detect cancer, grade tumours, count cells and find patterns linked to genetic changes or treatment response. Pathology foundation models trained on millions of images are emerging. The first step for any pathology department is digitisation itself, scanners, storage and workflow, since AI only works on digital slides. For drugmakers, the same models help discover biomarkers and select trial patients, which is why pathology AI companies work closely with pharma.
